title: Correspondence coloring graphs with a forbidden clique
main_claim: For fixed r>=4, every K_r-free graph with sufficiently large maximum degree Delta has chi_DP <= ceil(C_r Delta/log Delta). This gives the Alon-Krivelevich-Sudakov conjecture for every forbidden subgraph F, in correspondence form.
coverage:
I read all sections: adjustment, triangles, rounds and completion. I checked each step by hand.
(1) LP-duality reduction: the cone is closed; the drop test gives eq. drop-test; the bad-vertex triangle bound is O(Lambda^2) w_i y_i.
(2) Dyadic median-price levels: each good triangle survives at exactly one level, with the factor 12. Coefficient bounds 0<=beta<alpha<=2, kappa<=4, and kappa>=1 on retained edges. Level neighborhood bound 8Lambda.
(3) Sparse multiplier induction: means equal 1, edge-mass constants (1/4 + 1/2)eps s^2, and the multiplier bound.
(4) Local cross estimate: entropy bound f(1+a)<=a log(1+a); numerator/k' is O(e^{-6h}); the random left/right split handles overlapping sets. Transfer through edge-injective homomorphisms.
(5) Triangle section: middle-edge charge 2M_x; deletion losses O(M_x/l^2) and O(log l/l)M_x. Growth of D_j in mass and per-part count (<=e^{40l^2}<=P0) and its radius. Leakage induction. Two J_v applications of local cross. Mixture-entropy bound H_R=O(log l). Entropy-increment identity using stationarity. TV factor 2 through the intermediary row. Coupling disagreement 2d/(1+d). Markov bound for reverse-qualification. Split neighborhood weight <=e^{sqrt l}. Summability of losses across l -> sqrt l. Final bound e^X M_x.
(6) Rounds: first-order moments of Y_i, the entropy identity, and the drop cost <= Lambda w_i (log(w_*/w_i) <= ~2 log Delta < 20 log Delta). The expected potential change matches d_i + t_i + sum a_j g_i <= (B+1)d_i.
(7) Read-k concentration: Holder induction plus Hoeffding. Exponents Delta^{0.68} and Delta^{0.46}; participation P0 and 2P0.
(8) Host activation probability. Collision max-degree and matching tail (e mu/m)^m with mu=Delta^{0.8+o(1)}, m=Delta^{0.82}.
(9) LLL dependency radius and degree exp(O(log Delta loglog Delta)).
(10) Trimming costs: nonpositive above Delta^{-0.99}; o(xi) below Delta^{-3}; s_i>Lambda trims paid by edge loss. K/8 > B+1. The window W_v >= K - K/100 - o(1) follows from C=100K/gamma. Final degree Delta^{0.96} < (K/2)Delta^{0.99} available entries.
I found no failing step.
sibling_notes: Nothing was on the family-184 board before I posted. The paper says it adapts lemmas from the companion paper 'A logarithmic independence bound for clique-free graphs' (sparse multipliers, the cross estimate, entropy splitting). It re-proves all of them here, with radius and per-part participation conditions added, so it does not depend on that paper circularly. A sibling reviewing the companion paper could reuse this check of Lemmas 2.2-2.3 and Sections 3-5.
